newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo naphtha slips in thin market due to crude.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo naphtha slips in thin market due to crude.

text.p: Tokyo naphtha prices lost ground on Friday, tracking crude oil losses in a market made thin by the absence of many Asian traders for the Chinese New Year holiday, traders said.
"It (the decline) is simply on the back of crude, I think. The market is very thin because of the holiday," a trader said.
Open-spec naphtha second-half April was notionally assessed at $233.00/235.50, down about $5 from late Thursday levels, traders said.
First-half April was some $3 in backwardation at $236.00/238.50.
In spreads, the backwardation was notionally assessed wider, with first-half April/first-half May notionally assessed at $6 for bids and $7.50 for offers.

Two second-half April naphtha cargoes were believed to have changed hands at $240.50 late on Thursday. The cargoes are believed to have been purchased by Japanese and South Korean traders, but the identity of the sellers was unclear.

A mild winter in Japan and ample stocks were seen as major reasons for the slow market for kerosene, traders said. One trader said that a Japanese refinery might be tapping the market for kerosene cargo availability.--Tokyo Energy Desk
